narrative:
**Headline: a sharp downloads contraction alongside a spike in Spaces engagement.** Model downloads fell 23.2% week-over-week to 2,638,844 across the 25,923 tracked models, and were down 27.2% against four weeks ago — the clearest negative signal in the set. Model likes softened more modestly, down 6.8% to 7,961, though they held essentially flat on a four-week basis (+0.3%). Space likes moved the opposite way, rising 46.7% to 895 from a base of 6,475 Spaces, and up 47.3% over four weeks. The divergence between download volume and Spaces-side engagement is the week's main story; with only four-week history available (12-week deltas are null across all metrics), it is not yet possible to say whether the downloads drop is a trend break or normal volatility.

**Family mix shifted toward Gemma and the long tail, away from Llama.** Gemma-family models rose 23.2% to 1,009 and Mistral rose 15.6% to 193 (+78.9% over four weeks), while Llama fell 25.3% to 969. Qwen grew 8.3% to 6,016 but remained 19.0% below its level four weeks ago. "Other-open" was the largest labeled bucket at 8,850 (+11.9% w/w, +32.9% over four weeks). Kimi/Moonshot reached 78 models, a 254.5% weekly increase, but off a very small prior base (roughly 22) — treat the percentage as directional only. A significant methodology caveat: 8,436 models (32.6% of the total) carry an "unknown" family label, so family shares should be read as shares of the labeled subset. Within use cases, Qwen led coding at 36.1% of 155 Spaces (down 7.6%) and rose to 30.4% of 552 chat-assistant Spaces (+34.5%); DeepSeek's 121.4% jump in coding share translates to roughly 11 Spaces, so the absolute movement is small.

**On the Spaces side (full coverage, coverage = 1), creation patterns were mixed.** Image generation rose 9.7% to 734 and video generation 12.2% to 312, while chat-assistant fell 4.4% to 955 and coding dropped 16.9% to 212 — though coding is still up 48.2% over four weeks. SDK distribution held steady: static 3,718 (+0.1%), Gradio 2,145 (-1.0%), Docker 480 (-5.3%); Streamlit's 29.7% rise was off a base of 83. In technology penetration, quantized Spaces rose to 2.32% (+19.9% w/w) and local-inference to 2.69% (+25.2% over four weeks), while fine-tuned fell to 3.26% (-15.3%) and RAG to 2.41% (-7.6%). By vertical, scientific research rose to 8.48% (+14.3%) and consumer to 9.65% (+8.0%), while enterprise productivity (6.52%, -15.0%), healthcare (4.06%, -15.1%) and cybersecurity (2.13%, -22.8%) retreated — the latter two after four-week gains, so single-week reversals. Next week, watch whether model downloads stabilize or extend a third consecutive decline, and whether the Space-likes surge persists or proves to be a one-week spike.
